data.note:
My call of DNA replication was wrong; unblinded as lactacystin annotated as Protein degradation.

I over-weighted the NSC vote (2/4 DNA replication, e10) and bridging wells, and under-weighted that similarities were low (0.25) and per-well votes split including Kinase inhibitors and DNA damage. The high-dose enlarged cells with dim DNA and intact microtubules (e2, e4) plus monotonic cell-area increase (e12) fits proteasome-inhibition cytotoxicity/spreading rather than specific replication arrest, but I forced it into DNA replication.

Literature confirms lactacystin as 20S proteasome inhibitor context: e.g. PMID 39988264 describes delivery of 20S proteasome inhibitor lactacystin; PMID 18650992, PMID 21377449 study proteasome inhibitor lactacystin effects.

Follow-up I proposed (EdU + DNA-content flow) remains the right discriminator, plus a proteasome-activity assay and ubiquitin accumulation control.

reflection.text:
Unblinding showed lactacystin, a proteasome inhibitor (PMID 39988264) (PMID 21377449) (PMID 18650992), so the truth was Protein degradation while I concluded DNA replication at 0.45. The raw phenotypic trends I quantified were real: cell enlargement with dose (cell_area rho=+1.00) and falling mean/integrated DNA (rho=-1.00 from +5.4/+4.4 at 0.3 uM to -8.4 at 10 uM) with large high-dose effects (cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+9.3, nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4).

I was misled by the biphasic DNA split and by atlas matching. The mid-dose high-DNA well plus microscopist DNA-damage call anchored DNA damage/replication, then bridging wells at 1 uM and 3 uM both voted DNA replication for 2/4 NSC majority. I over-weighted that vote despite low similarities (0.165-0.317), single-replicate wells, and a post-unblinding literature search for proteasome cell-enlargement/low-DNA phenotype returning 0 hits, and I never held protein degradation as a live hypothesis.

The acquisition choice to bridge the DNA flip (high/mid then 1 and 3 uM) reinforced the same imaging bias instead of testing an orthogonal mechanism. Lesson: for enlarged low-DNA cells with intact tubulin/actin and no mitotic increase, proteasome/protein-homeostasis must be explicitly tested with ubiquitin and activity readouts, not decided by NSC vote alone.
what_was_right: Detected monotonic dose-dependent cell enlargement (e12 cell_area rho=+1.00, e8-e9 cell_nuc_area_ratio +4.2 to +5.7, e2 +9.3) and falling DNA intensity/integrated DNA (e11/e14 rho=-1.00).
Recognized the low- vs high-dose discordance (e3 nuc_dna_mean +5.4 at 0.3 uM vs e2 -8.4 at 10 uM) and acquired bridging 1 and 3 uM wells to test it.

Correctly down-weighted Aurora/Eg5/microtubule classes based on lack of mitotic/multinucleate phenotype and kept probability calibrated at 0.45 with low atlas similarities 0.165-0.317 and single replicates.
what_was_wrong: Interpreted low-dose DNA-high to high-dose DNA-low plus enlargement as replication stress/DNA damage rather than proteasome-inhibition growth arrest with enlarged cells and reduced DNA staining.
Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas NSC 2/4 DNA replication vote (e10) and k-neighbour Aurora/DNA-replication counts despite low similarity, allowing it to drive the conclusion rationale.

Never generated protein-degradation evidence: no ubiquitin/p62, proteasome-activity, or cell-cycle profile acquisition; second literature search for proteasome enlargement phenotype returned 0 hits (e19) and was not followed up.
Bridging acquisitions at 1 uM (e8) and 3 uM (e9) sampled the same morphological axis and reinforced atlas bias instead of a discriminative test of replication (EdU/S-phase) vs proteasome blockade.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 7: DNA damage 0.28, DNA replication 0.22, Kinase inhibitors 0.20, Protein synthesis 0.15, Cholesterol-lowering 0.15
- after step 15: DNA replication 0.45, DNA damage 0.25, Kinase inhibitors 0.12, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10, Cholesterol-lowering 0.08

## Conclusion

**DNA replication** (stated probability 0.45); key evidence e10, e8, e9, e11, e3.

Why: NSC 2/4 DNA replication with bridging 1 and 3 uM both voting it; low-dose high-DNA to high-dose low-DNA plus enlargement trend fits replication stress.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Pulse-EdU incorporation with DNA-content flow cytometry plus tubulin counterstain across 0.3-10 uM to test S-phase suppression vs G2 accumulation and confirm intact microtubules.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Approve DNA replication (0.45) as best-supported, not certain. The 4-point trend (e11/e14: DNA mean/integrated from +5.4/+4.4 at 0.3 uM to -8.4/-6.8 at 10 uM, rho=-1.00; e12 cell area rho=+1.00) plus intact tubulin/actin and no mitotic/multinucleate increase (e4/e5) argues against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule/actin classes despite neighbor counts. NSC bridging wells at 1 and 3 uM both vote DNA replication (e8-e10), while DNA damage (0.25) explains only the single 0.3 uM DNA-high well (e3/e5) and kinase (0.12) only the 10 uM well (e6). Acquisitions were discriminative: high/mid then bridging the DNA flip. All wells are single-replicate and atlas similarities are low (0.165-0.317, vote 2/4), so 0.45 is calibrated; the monotonic multi-dose coherence mitigates single-well risk and no further affordable imaging well would molecularly separate replication from damage.

## Unblinding

Compound: **lactacystin** (PubChem CID [6610292](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6610292))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

Unblinding showed lactacystin, a proteasome inhibitor (PMID 39988264) (PMID 21377449) (PMID 18650992), so the truth was Protein degradation while I concluded DNA replication at 0.45. The raw phenotypic trends I quantified were real: cell enlargement with dose (cell_area rho=+1.00) and falling mean/integrated DNA (rho=-1.00 from +5.4/+4.4 at 0.3 uM to -8.4 at 10 uM) with large high-dose effects (cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+9.3, nuc_dna_mean z=-8.4).

I was misled by the biphasic DNA split and by atlas matching. The mid-dose high-DNA well plus microscopist DNA-damage call anchored DNA damage/replication, then bridging wells at 1 uM and 3 uM both voted DNA replication for 2/4 NSC majority. I over-weighted that vote despite low similarities (0.165-0.317), single-replicate wells, and a post-unblinding literature search for proteasome cell-enlargement/low-DNA phenotype returning 0 hits, and I never held protein degradation as a live hypothesis.

The acquisition choice to bridge the DNA flip (high/mid then 1 and 3 uM) reinforced the same imaging bias instead of testing an orthogonal mechanism. Lesson: for enlarged low-DNA cells with intact tubulin/actin and no mitotic increase, proteasome/protein-homeostasis must be explicitly tested with ubiquitin and activity readouts, not decided by NSC vote alone.

What was right:
- Detected monotonic dose-dependent cell enlargement (e12 cell_area rho=+1.00, e8-e9 cell_nuc_area_ratio +4.2 to +5.7, e2 +9.3) and falling DNA intensity/integrated DNA (e11/e14 rho=-1.00).
- Recognized the low- vs high-dose discordance (e3 nuc_dna_mean +5.4 at 0.3 uM vs e2 -8.4 at 10 uM) and acquired bridging 1 and 3 uM wells to test it.
- Correctly down-weighted Aurora/Eg5/microtubule classes based on lack of mitotic/multinucleate phenotype and kept probability calibrated at 0.45 with low atlas similarities 0.165-0.317 and single replicates.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted low-dose DNA-high to high-dose DNA-low plus enlargement as replication stress/DNA damage rather than proteasome-inhibition growth arrest with enlarged cells and reduced DNA staining.
- Over-weighted compare_to_reference_atlas NSC 2/4 DNA replication vote (e10) and k-neighbour Aurora/DNA-replication counts despite low similarity, allowing it to drive the conclusion rationale.
- Never generated protein-degradation evidence: no ubiquitin/p62, proteasome-activity, or cell-cycle profile acquisition; second literature search for proteasome enlargement phenotype returned 0 hits (e19) and was not followed up.
- Bridging acquisitions at 1 uM (e8) and 3 uM (e9) sampled the same morphological axis and reinforced atlas bias instead of a discriminative test of replication (EdU/S-phase) vs proteasome blockade.

Proposed next experiment: Across 0.03-10 uM lactacystin vs DMSO and a DNA-replication control, measure chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity plus anti-ubiquitin/p62 accumulation in parallel with EdU pulse and DNA-content flow to test proteasome blockade with secondary cell-cycle arrest versus direct S-phase suppression.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [39988264](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39988264/): GDNF reduces fibril-induced early-stage alpha-synuclein pathology after delivery of 20S proteasome inhibitor lactacystin. *Eur J Pharm Sci* (2025) — Lactacystin is a 20S proteasome inhibitor, consistent with protein degradation as the true MoA.
- PMID [21377449](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21377449/): Lactacystin, a proteasome inhibitor, enhances BMP-induced osteoblastic differentiation by increasing active Smads. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun* (2011) — Lactacystin is described as a proteasome inhibitor.
- PMID [18650992](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18650992/): The proteasome inhibitor lactacystin attenuates growth and migration of vascular smooth muscle cells and limits the response to arterial injury. *Exp Clin Cardiol* (2007) — The proteasome inhibitor lactacystin attenuates growth, consistent with the observed cell loss and lower density.
